hook: "Your best static ads have a ceiling."
body: A tool/skill pitch: drop in your best static ad and get back a 6-second stop-motion version as video. The argument: statics have a ceiling (no video slots, no autoplay), and the creative already validated the concept — this just removes the distribution ceiling. 6s demo video attached.
cta: "Sauce in the article below" — link to the method.
idea: Animate the winner: a validated static becomes a 6-second stop-motion video, unlocking video placements without new creative risk.
sequencing: Problem: best statics have a ceiling (no video slots/autoplay).
Solution: the skill — static in, 6s stop-motion video out.
Logic: the creative already did the hard part and validated the concept.
Job now: distribution, not ideation.
CTA: the article with the method.
formatting: Short text + 6s demo video. Tool-pitch voice.
why_it_works: "The creative did the hard part already" reframes the tool as risk-free leverage on a proven winner rather than another thing to test.
what_to_steal: The pipeline step for LC: every winning static auto-generates a 6s stop-motion version on the same day — double the placements, zero new concepts, and the concept risk is already retired.

product: commentary — no product (YouTube Shorts playbook; Higgsfield MCP)
hook: "YouTube Shorts is the most underpriced ad inventory in Google right now and 90% of ecom brands STILL aren't running a single ad there"
body: A YouTube Shorts arbitrage playbook: Shorts is the most underpriced Google inventory; the blocker ("we don't have video") dies via Higgsfield MCP in Claude (Seedance 2.0, Kling 3.0, Veo 3.1). The 6-second play: unskippable bumpers — no skip button, full message seen, penny CPVs. Includes the exact prompt for turning a product image into a 6s vertical bumper and a 15s Shorts ad structure (hook frame → product reveal → social proof → CTA).
cta: DM "SHORTS" for a brand-specific setup walkthrough.
idea: Repurpose winning Meta statics into 6-second unskippable Shorts bumpers via AI video — the cheapest new-customer channel nobody's bidding on.
sequencing: Arbitrage: Shorts = most underpriced Google inventory.
Blocker: "we don't have video creative."
Unlock: Higgsfield MCP in Claude, 60-second setup.
The 6s play: unskippable bumpers — full message, penny views.
Prompts: product image → 6s bumper; lifestyle image generation for CTR.
Structure: 15s Shorts ad (hook → reveal → proof → CTA).
Targeting: custom intent from category searches.
CTA: DM "SHORTS."
formatting: Long playbook thread with copy-paste prompts; one photo. Step-by-step.
why_it_works: "Unskippable" + "pennies" + "90% aren't there" is a three-part arbitrage pitch, and the copy-paste prompts remove the execution excuse.
what_to_steal: The 6s bumper prompt as LC's YouTube line: winning jewelry statics → 6s unskippable bumpers (water beading, stack reveal) aimed at custom-intent "waterproof jewelry" searchers — a channel LC likely isn't bidding.

product: commentary — no product (HookMaster AI MCP demo on a Brezza S-CNG ad)
hook: "OMG! Claude can finally watch and analyze video ads."
body: A product demo of HookMaster AI inside Claude: it watched a 20-second Brezza S-CNG ad (starring Kartik Aaryan) frame by frame and found the entire sale happens in 3 seconds — celebrity opening earns attention, product appears in the first 5s, underbody S-CNG positioning answers a real buyer concern. It flagged the 0:13 driving montage as the weakest moment and recommended a 6-second cutdown for skippable placements.
cta: "What ad should I make Claude analyze next?" (reply bait) + full analysis in the reply.
idea: Frame-by-frame AI critique finds the 3 seconds that sell and the montage that wastes — then prescribes the 6-second cutdown.
sequencing: Hook: Claude can watch video ads now.
Setup: HookMaster MCP + 20s Brezza ad with Kartik Aaryan.
Finding: the entire sale happens in 3 seconds.
Why it works: celebrity open → product in 5s → positioning answers a concern.
Weakness: generic montage at 0:13.
Prescription: 6-second cutdown for skippable.
CTA: what ad next?
formatting: Demo post + 35s video + analysis photo. AI-capability flex.
why_it_works: A celebrity ad getting a ruthless AI grade is inherently watchable, and the "3 seconds" finding gives every reader a new lens for their own creatives.
what_to_steal: The 3-second-sale audit for LC: run every jewelry creative through the "where does the sale happen" test — if the waterproof proof isn't inside 5 seconds, cut the montage and ship the 6s version.

hook: "this client went viral with our brolls"
body: A UGC agency's viral formula: viral hook in your niche + 4-6 second shocked reaction vid + a demo of your app/website ("the demo format in the video is going viral rn") = done. Claims a client went viral with their B-rolls.
idea: The 3-part viral micro-structure: niche hook + 4-6s shocked reaction + product demo — that's the whole ad.
sequencing: Proof: client went viral with our B-rolls.
Part 1: viral hook in your niche.
Part 2: 4-6 second shocked reaction vid.
Part 3: demo of your app/website.
Close: "its that easy, try it out."
why_it_works: "Its that easy" plus a 3-part recipe makes virality feel like assembly, which is exactly what a time-starved operator wants to believe.
what_to_steal: The micro-structure for LC's shortest creatives: hook ("my $12 necklace turned my neck green") + 4-6s shocked reaction + 6s waterproof demo — the entire ad in under 15 seconds.

hook: "Every lab claims 'we're the best model' and the phrase means nothing the moment you actually make something."
body: A model-ranking argument: "best model" is meaningless — best at cinematic film look ≠ best at 6-second ads ≠ lipsync ≠ cleanup. OpenArt Arena ranks models by the actual jobs creatives do, judged blind by working people. The useful question is "best at what." 13s video attached.
idea: Judge AI models by job (6-second ads, lipsync, cleanup), blind, by working creatives — not by demo reels.
sequencing: Problem: "best model" claims collapse in production.
Truth: different jobs need different models.
Solution: OpenArt Arena, blind judging by working people.
The question: never "best" — "best at what."
CTA: the rankings.
formatting: Short text + 13s video + link. Contrarian take.
why_it_works: "Best at what" is a portable mental tool that flatters the reader's sophistication while demolishing lazy vendor claims.
what_to_steal: The procurement rule for LC's AI pipeline: benchmark video models on the 6-second jewelry demo job specifically (water realism, metal reflections) — never buy on cinematic demo reels.

product: Smooche color-changing foundation (ad described, not the poster's product)
hook: "One ad that has 12 duplicates and has been running for 225 days. And it is not 2 mins long. Nop. I think it is 6 seconds long"
body: A competitor teardown of Smooche's shortest winner: a ~6-second foundation clip with 12 duplicates running 225 days. The whole ad is one readable headline over product-in-use footage: "omg I think I finally found a foundation that looks like second skin." The thesis: fried audiences won't watch 2 minutes without a story, so short product-in-use clips win. Includes the ad link and lander (smooche.com/products/color-changing-foundation).
cta: The ad's implied CTA: the product page link.
idea: The 6-second product-in-use clip with one readable headline can outlive every long-form ad in the account — 225 days, 12 duplicates.
sequencing: Brand: Smooche scaling hard into Q4.
Funnel note: cross-sells, bundles, add-ons capture max per visitor.
The specimen: 6s clip, 12 duplicates, 225 days.
The headline: "omg I think I finally found a foundation that looks like second skin."
Thesis: fried brains won't watch 2 minutes without a story.
Mechanism: short product-in-use clips.
Proof links: the ad + the lander.
Aside: their Shopify payments rant.
formatting: Long casual teardown post with ad + lander links. Conversational, profane.
why_it_works: 225 days × 12 duplicates is an undeniable receipt, and the "fried brain" thesis gives media buyers permission to stop overproducing.
what_to_steal: The exact LC adaptation: a 6-second clip of water beading off a necklace (or a stack going into the pool) with one headline — "omg I think I finally found jewelry that survives the pool" — run as the evergreen micro-demo for 200+ days.

hook: "I created this cozy 6-second lo-fi loop animation entirely within @adobefirefly"
body: A sponsored Adobe demo (#Ad, #AdobeFireflyAmbassadors): a cozy 6-second lo-fi loop animation made entirely in Adobe Firefly — illustration + animation + AI-generated music matched to mood/style/tempo, layered in one workflow.
idea: One tool, one workflow: illustration, animation, and mood-matched AI music for a seamless 6-second loop.
sequencing: The make: 6s lo-fi loop, entirely in Firefly.
Step 1: illustration + animation.
Step 2: AI music matched to mood/style/tempo.
Step 3: layer music over animation.
Love: visuals + music in one workflow.
CTA: try Firefly.
formatting: Short sponsored text + 21s video. Warm, process-sharing tone.
why_it_works: "Entirely within" one tool is the pitch — no pipeline, no handoffs — and the cozy loop is engineered for the rewatch metric the algo loves.
what_to_steal: The loop + mood-matched music combo for LC's ambient placements (stories, reels backgrounds): a 6s jewelry loop (chain swaying, water rippling) with matched audio — cheap, hypnotic, infinitely rewatchable.
